answer: Sybil resistance starts with staking identity to scarce, verifiable resources rather than cheap registrations. Picture an economy as a garden: each agent must plant a bond—locked capital, compute hours, or real attestation history—before it earns a voice. New entrants grow like seedlings at the edge of a lagoon, gated by one trusted peer who countersigns them and stakes reputation on that signature. A sybil farm then has to duplicate a pearl: costly, slow, and traceable, because every false copy dilutes the very stake the attacker spent to create it.
